The apps now notice when you lock the computer, and offer to resume after an unanswered check-in.

## Download

- **macOS 13 or newer** (Apple Silicon and Intel): [TasksBar.zip](https://github.com/Astervista/tasks/releases/download/v2.1.1/TasksBar.zip)
- **Windows** (64-bit): [TasksTray.exe](https://github.com/Astervista/tasks/releases/download/v2.1.1/TasksTray.exe)

The apps aren't signed yet, so your system will warn you the first time:

- **macOS:** unzip, move `TasksBar.app` to Applications (replacing the old one), then run this once:
  ```sh
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/TasksBar.app
  ```
- **Windows:** choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

## What's fixed

- **Locking counts as leaving:** the lock key, ⌃⌘Q or the display turning off on macOS, and Win+L on Windows, now pause the running task as of that moment. Before, only real sleep did, and a locked computer that stayed awake kept the timer running until the check-in stopped it. Unlocking shows the "Welcome back" window to resume it.
- **Unanswered check-ins offer to resume:** when nobody answers "how far along?", the task is still paused as of the question, and now the "Welcome back" window appears as soon as the keyboard or mouse is used again.
- The "Welcome back" window says why the task was paused.

## Upgrading

- **Server:** nothing changed; no update needed.
- **Command line tool:** only the version number changed. To update it anyway:
  ```sh
  git pull && npm ci && npm run cli:install
  ```
